                                   PUC PROJECT NO. 58000

 RULEMAKING TO UPDATE                             §              BEFORE THE
 WHOLESALE AND IOU RETAIL                         §      PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION
 TRANSMISSION COST RECOVERY                       §
 IN THE ERCOT REGION                              §                OF TEXAS


     JOINT COMMENTS OF AUSTIN ENERGY, BANDERA ELECTRIC, BRAZOS
          ELECTRIC, CPS ENERGY, AND STEC IN PROJECT NO. 58000

TO THE HONORABLE PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION OF TEXAS:

       The City of Austin d/b/a Austin Energy (Austin Energy), Bandera Electric Cooperative,

Inc. (Bandera Electric), Brazos Electric Power Cooperative, Inc. (Brazos Electric), CPS Energy,

and South Texas Electric Cooperative, Inc. (STEC) (together, the Public Power Utilities) submit

these Joint Comments to the Public Utility Commission of Texas (Commission) in Project No.

58000. On June 12, 2026, Commission Staff filed proposed amendments to existing 16 Texas

Administrative Code (TAC) §§ 25.192 and 25.193, relating to Transmission Service Rates and to

Distribution Service Provider Transmission Cost Recovery Factors (TCRF), respectively. On July 2,

2026, Commission Staff filed a Proposal for Publication with an August 11, 2026, deadline for

public comments and then filed a revised Proposal for Publication on July 9, 2026. The Public

Power Utilities appreciate the opportunity to comment on Commission Staff’s Recommendation

in this rulemaking and timely submit the following.


                        I.      COMMENTS ON 16 TAC § 25.192(c)(2)

       The Public Power Utilities oppose the application of proposed 16 TAC § 25.192(c)(2) to

non-investor-owned utility (Non-IOU) transmission service providers (TSPs). The proposed

requirement is unsupported by the Commission’s jurisdiction over Non-IOU TSPs, counter to

Commission precedent, inconsistent with the statutory framework established under the Public



Public Power Utilities Joint Comments in Project No. 58000                            Page 1 of 9
 Utility Regulatory Act (PURA), and unrelated to the stated purpose of this rulemaking. The Public

Power Utilities urge the Commission to remove 16 TAC § 25.192(c)(2) and wholesale

transmission service at distribution voltage definitions from the proposed rule. At minimum, the

Commission should expressly exempt Non-IOU TSPs for the reasons discussed below.


a.      Application of 16 TAC § 25.192(c)(2) to Non-IOU TSPs is Inconsistent with PURA

        The Commission’s limited jurisdiction over Non-IOU TSPs—namely, Municipally Owned

Utilities (MOUs) and electric cooperatives—is well established. The Texas Supreme Court has

expressly recognized that PURA Chapter 35 does not grant the Commission general rate oversight

capacity over MOUs. In Texas Municipal Power Agency v. Public Utility Commission of Texas,

the Court declared that “[n]owhere does PURA chapter 35 give the Commission general rate

oversight capacity” and characterized the Commission’s role with respect to wholesale distribution

service as “largely an oversight role.” 1 Similarly, in Public Utility Commission of Texas v. City

Public Service Board, the Court held that “the Commission’s jurisdiction over municipally owned

utilities is restricted” and that, “[u]nlike investor-owned utilities, municipally owned utilities retain

the ability to set their own rates without the Commission’s approval.” 2 The same applies to electric

cooperatives, which also retain authority to set their own rates without Commission approval.

        PURA’s statutory framework reinforces these jurisdictional limitations. Under PURA

§ 40.055(a)(1), a municipal governing body retains “exclusive jurisdiction” to “set all terms of

access, conditions, and rates applicable to services provided by the municipally owned utility . . .

including nondiscriminatory and comparable rates for distribution.” 3 Similarly, under PURA


        1
                Texas Mun. Power Agency v. Pub. Util. Comm’n of Texas, 253 S.W.3d 184, 194 (Tex. 2007).
        2
                Public Util. Comm’n v. City Pub. Serv. Bd., 53 S.W.3d 310, 318 (Tex. 2001).
        3
                PURA § 40.055(a)(1).



Public Power Utilities Joint Comments in Project No. 58000                                      Page 2 of 9
 § 41.055(1), an electric cooperative’s board of directors retains “exclusive jurisdiction” to “set all

terms of access, conditions, and rates applicable to services provided by the electric

cooperative . . . including nondiscriminatory and comparable rates for distribution.” 4                          The

Commission’s authority over wholesale transmission service at distribution voltage for MOUs and

electric cooperatives is therefore limited to ensuring open access and comparable terms pursuant

to PURA § 35.004(a)—not to conducting cost of service ratemaking for distribution facilities or

distribution level service. 5

         Proposed 16 TAC § 25.192(c)(2) oversteps the Commission’s jurisdictional limits in

Chapter 35 of PURA by inserting wholesale transmission service at distribution-voltage tariff

requirements into 16 TAC § 25.192, the rule governing Transmission Cost of Service (TCOS)

proceedings. In doing so, the proposed requirement improperly conflates two distinct regulatory

proceedings that are governed by separate rules, serve different purposes, and derive from separate

statutory authorities. 6 The Commission itself has expressly recognized this distinction, stating that

“[a] tariff for wholesale transmission service at distribution voltage under 16 TAC § 25.191 differs

from a tariff for transmission service under 16 TAC § 25.192.” 7 Respectfully, Commission Staff’s

cooperatives, to “provide wholesale transmission service at rates and terms, including terms of access, that are
comparable to the rates and terms of the utility's own use of its system,” but not granting the Commission cost of
service ratemaking authority over such service); see also Application of the City of San Antonio, Acting By and
Through the City Public Service Board, to Amend its Wholesale Transmission Customer Primary Distribution Voltage
Service Tariff, Docket No. 51409, Order at Conclusion of Law No. 12 (Sep. 15, 2022) (confirming that CPS Energy's
wholesale transmission service at distribution voltage is provided “in accordance with PURA § 35.004(a) and 16 TAC
§ 25.191(d)(2),” not under 16 TAC § 25.192's cost of service framework).
         6
                  See 16 TAC § 25.191(d)(2)(C) (requiring a DSP to file a tariff for wholesale transmission service at
distribution voltage as a standalone proceeding, separate from any TCOS application under § 25.192); see also
Application of Medina Electric Cooperative, Inc., For Approval of a Wholesale Transmission Service at Distribution
Voltage Tariff Under 16 TAC § 25.191 (d)(2)(C), Docket No. 51606, Order at Conclusions of Law Nos. 5, 10–14 (Oct.
20, 2022) (addressing wholesale distribution service exclusively under 16 TAC § 25.191 and expressly distinguishing
the proceeding from TCOS rate review under § 25.192).
         7
                  Docket No. 51409, Preliminary Order at 2 (Jun. 14, 2021).



Public Power Utilities Joint Comments in Project No. 58000                                               Page 3 of 9
 proposed inclusion of 16 TAC § 25.192(c)(2) is at odds with PURA, Texas Supreme Court

precedent, and prior Commission interpretations of PURA, and would improperly expand the

scope of a TCOS proceeding beyond the Commission’s statutory bounds.


b.       16 TAC § 25.192(c)(2) Conflicts with Over Twenty Years of Commission Precedent

         For more than two decades, the Commission has segregated full TCOS cases from

proceedings addressing wholesale distribution service rates for electric cooperatives and MOUs.

The Commission has never required a Non-IOU TSP to include wholesale distribution rates as a

prerequisite to administrative completeness in a TCOS case. 8 This longstanding practice is

Docket No. 55568, Commission Order No. 3 at 1 (Dec. 11, 2023) (same); Application of Bandera Electric
Cooperative, Inc. for Approval of a Wholesale Transmission Service at Distribution Voltage Tariff Under 16 TAC §
25.191(d)(2)(C), Docket No. 53817, Commission Order No. 2 at 1 (Aug. 15, 2022) (same); Application of Medina
Electric Cooperative, Inc. For a Wholesale Transmission Service at Distribution Voltage Tariff Under 16 TAC §

Cooperative Association dba PenTex Energy for Approval of a Wholesale Transmission Service at Distribution
Voltage Tariff Under 16 TAC § 25.191(d)(2)(C), Docket No. 50037, Notice Addressing Application and Notice
Sufficiency, and Establishing Procedural Schedule at 1 (Oct. 23, 2019) (same); Application of Victoria Electric


Public Power Utilities Joint Comments in Project No. 58000                                              Page 4 of 9
 reflected in numerous dockets involving CPS Energy, Brazos Electric, Bluebonnet Electric

Cooperative, Pedernales Electric Cooperative, Taylor Electric Cooperative, and Trinity Valley

Electric Cooperative, among others. 9 As drafted, the proposed rule departs from this settled

framework without identifying a statutory basis, policy need, or changed circumstance warranting

such a departure.


c.      16 TAC § 25.192(c)(2) is Inconsistent with the Existing Regulatory Structure

        16 TAC § 25.192 is a TCOS rule, and its cost-recovery framework is limited to facilities

eligible for inclusion in transmission rates—generally facilities operated at 60 kilovolts or above,

subject only to narrow exceptions such as capacitors and other reactive devices located in a

distribution substation. 10 By contrast, wholesale transmission service provided at distribution

voltage is separately addressed in 16 TAC § 25.191, which governs wholesale service provided

through facilities rated below 60 kV and requires a separate tariff for that service. 11 Proposed 16

TAC § 25.192(c)(2) would therefore import a distinct distribution-voltage service into a TCOS

proceeding, even though the underlying facilities and rates are not recoverable through a TCOS


Cooperative, Inc. for Approval of a Wholesale Transmission Service at Distribution Voltage Tariff Under 16 TAC §
25.191(d)(2), Docket No. 49201, Order Addressing Application and Notice Sufficiency, and Establishing Procedural
Schedule at 1 (Feb. 25, 2019); Application of Denton County Electric Cooperative, Inc. dba CoServ Electric for
Approval of Wholesale Transmission Service at Distribution Voltage and Generation Export Service Tariff, Docket
No. 47682, Notice Addressing Sufficiency of Application, Establishing Procedural Schedule, Requiring Clarification
on Notice at 1 (Nov. 8, 2017) (same); Application of Farmers Electric Cooperative, Inc. for Wholesale Distribution
Service (WDS) Tariff, Docket No. 47551, Notice Addressing Sufficiency and Notice, Establishing Procedural
Schedule at 1 (Sep. 18, 2017) (same); Application of Taylor Electric Cooperative, Inc. for Approval of Wholesale
Distribution Tariff, Docket No. 36026, Notice of Approval at 1 (Sep. 18, 2008) (approving WDS tariff without
discussion of TCOS rates).
        9
                  Id. (citing wholesale distribution service tariff proceedings filed and processed as standalone
applications under 16 TAC § 25.191(d)(2)(C), without a corresponding TCOS filing).
        10
                 16 TAC § 25.192(c)(1).
        11
                   16 TAC § 25.191(d)(2)(A)–(C) (addressing wholesale transmission service provided at distribution
voltage through facilities rated below 60 kV); see also 16 TAC § 25.192(c)(1) (defining “transmission facilities”
eligible for TCOS cost recovery as those “operated at 60 kilovolts or above,” thereby excluding distribution-voltage
facilities from the § 25.192 framework).



Public Power Utilities Joint Comments in Project No. 58000                                             Page 5 of 9
 proceeding. 12 In effect, the proposal would make a separately governed tariff a prerequisite to

administrative completeness in a TCOS proceeding. It would also require inclusion of a tariff

governed by a different rule subject to different jurisdictional standards, and—for MOUs and

electric cooperatives—involving rates set by a governing body different than the Commission.

The result would create regulatory confusion, blur the jurisdictional boundaries clearly established

by PURA, and purport to expand the Commission’s role beyond the authority recognized by the

Legislature and Texas courts.


d.      16 TAC § 25.192(c)(2) Exceeds the Scope of This Rulemaking

        The stated purpose of Project No. 58000 is to implement Senate Bill (SB) 6 by replacing

the 4CP methodology with the 12CP methodology for assigning transmission costs. 13 Wholesale

transmission service at distribution voltage has no connection to the 4CP-to-12CP transition,

minimum billing demand for large load customers, or any other SB 6 provision. Proposed 16 TAC

§ 25.192(c)(2) does not implement, facilitate, or conform to the statutory changes this rulemaking

is intended to address. Instead, it introduces a substantive and jurisdictionally fraught requirement

unrelated to the rulemaking’s purpose. It does not belong here.


                II.      RECOMMENDED REVISION TO 16 TAC § 25.192(c)(2)

        Should the Commission decline to remove proposed 16 TAC § 25.192(c)(2) in its entirety,

as well as definitions related to wholesale transmission service at distribution voltage, the Public



        12
                 See 16 TAC § 25.191(d)(2) (which generally requires transmission service providers to provide
nondiscriminatory wholesale transmission service over distribution facilities, but does not grant the Commission the
same comprehensive ratemaking authority over an MOU’s wholesale distribution service rates that it exercises over
IOUs under PURA chapter 36); see also 16 TAC § 25.192(c) (addressing TCOS filings).
        13
                  Project No. 58000, Proposal for Publication of Amendments to § 25.192 and § 25.193 for
Consideration at the June 18, 2026 Open Meeting at 1.



Public Power Utilities Joint Comments in Project No. 58000                                             Page 6 of 9
 Power Utilities respectfully recommend that the rule expressly exempt Non-IOU TSPs, and

propose the following revision:

       (2)     If the TSP provides wholesale transmission service at distribution voltage,

       the tariff required by this section must include a separate section to reflect

       wholesale transmission service at distribution voltage rates, terms, and conditions

       set by the commission. A TSP must file an application to establish such tariff within

       30 days of receiving a request for such service. This requirement does not apply

       to Non-IOU TSPs.


       This exemption is necessary because a TCOS proceeding under 16 TAC § 25.192 is not

the equivalent of an IOU general rate case. Non-IOU TSPs are not subject to the Commission’s

comprehensive ratemaking authority under PURA Chapter 36 and instead remain subject to the

limited nondiscriminatory open-access requirements of PURA Chapter 35. Requiring Non-IOU

TSPs to include distribution-voltage tariffs in their TCOS proceedings would exceed the

Commission’s ratemaking authority and undermine the distinct regulatory framework PURA

establishes for MOUs and electric cooperatives.


                                      III.    CONCLUSION

       For the foregoing reasons, the Public Power Utilities respectfully request that the

Commission strike proposed 16 TAC § 25.192(c)(2) from the rule. Alternatively, the Commission

should expressly exempt Non-IOU TSPs from the rule’s requirements. Wholesale transmission

service at distribution voltage remains properly governed by 16 TAC § 25.191 and should continue

to be addressed in separate proceedings as longstanding Commission practice dictates. The

Commission has never established such a requirement through either its adjudicative proceedings



Public Power Utilities Joint Comments in Project No. 58000                               Page 7 of 9
 or longstanding practice. To the extent the Commission wishes to revisit the regulatory framework

for wholesale distribution service, it should do so through a separate rulemaking project with

appropriate notice and opportunity for comment—not through a provision embedded in a

rulemaking whose stated purpose is the implementation of SB 6.

                                    EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

Submitted by: City of Austin d/b/a Austin Energy (Austin Energy), Bandera Electric Cooperative,
Inc. (Bandera Electric), Brazos Electric Power Cooperative, Inc. (Brazos Electric), CPS Energy,
and South Texas Electric Cooperative, Inc. (STEC) (together, the Public Power Utilities).

The Public Power Utilities make the following substantive recommendations:

   •    Strike proposed 16 TAC § 25.192(c)(2) in its entirety; and

   •    Strike proposed definitions related to wholesale transmission service at distribution
        voltage, including proposed 16 TAC §§ 25.192(b)(15)(16).

In the alternative, should the Commission decline to remove the aforementioned sections, the
Public Power Utilities recommend the following:

    •   Add to the end of 16 TAC § 25.192(c)(2), “This requirement does not apply to Non-IOU
        TSPs.”

c.       16 TAC § 25.192(c)(2) is Inconsistent with the Existing Regulatory Structure

         16 TAC § 25.192 is a TCOS rule, and its cost-recovery framework is limited to facilities

eligible for inclusion in transmission rates-generally facilities operated at 60 kilovolts or above,

subj ect only to narrow exceptions such as capacitors and other reactive devices located in a

distribution substation.10 By contrast, wholesale transmission service provided at distribution

voltage is separately addressed in 16 TAC § 25.191, which governs wholesale service provided

through facilities rated below 60 kV and requires a separate tariff for that service. 11 Proposed 16

TAC § 25.192(c)(2) would therefore import a distinct distribution-voltage service into a TCOS

proceeding, even though the underlying facilities and rates are not recoverable through a TCOS

d.       16 TAC § 25.192(c)(2) Exceeds the Scope of This Rulemaking

        The stated purpose of Project No. 58000 is to implement Senate Bill (SB) 6 by replacing

the 4CP methodology with the 12CP methodology for assigning transmission costs. 13 Wholesale

transmission service at distribution voltage has no connection to the 4CP-to-12CP transition,

minimum billing demand for large load customers, or any other SB 6 provision. Proposed 16 TAC

§ 25.192(c)(2) does not implement, facilitate, or conform to the statutory changes this rulemaking

is intended to address. Instead, it introduces a substantive and jurisdictionally fraught requirement

unrelated to the rulemaking's purpose. It does not belong here.

       (2)     If the TSP provides wholesale transmission service at distribution voltage,

       the tariff required by this section must include a separate section to reflect

       wholesale transmission service at distribution voltage rates, terms, and conditions

       set by the commission. A TSP must file an application to establish such tariff within

       30 days of receiving a request for such service. This requirement does not apply

       to Non-IOU TSPs.


       This exemption is necessary because a TCOS proceeding under 16 TAC § 25.192 is not

the equivalent of an IOU general rate case. Non-IOU TSPs are not subject to the Commission's

comprehensive ratemaking authority under PURA Chapter 36 and instead remain subj ect to the

limited nondiscriminatory open-access requirements of PURA Chapter 35. Requiring Non-IOU

TSPs to include distribution-voltage tariffs in their TCOS proceedings would exceed the

Commission's ratemaking authority and undermine the distinct regulatory framework PURA

establishes for MOUs and electric cooperatives.


                                      III.    CONCLUSION

       For the foregoing reasons, the Public Power Utilities respectfully request that the

Commission strike proposed 16 TAC § 25.192(c)(2) from the rule. Alternatively, the Commission

should expressly exempt Non-IOU TSPs from the rule' s requirements. Wholesale transmission

service at distribution voltage remains properly governed by 16 TAC § 25.191 and should continue

to be addressed in separate proceedings as longstanding Commission practice dictates.          The

Commission has never established such a requirement through either its adjudicative proceedings
